title: VAKRA: Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Across APIs and Retrieval Under Tool-Use Policies

visual_explainer.question: Where do agents fail when a task requires multi-hop reasoning across executable APIs and document retrieval under tool-use policies?
visual_explainer.takeaway: VAKRA evaluates executable cross-source trajectories under a fixed agent harness and finds that the difficult boundary is often language-mediated entity and evidence grounding rather than API invocation syntax alone.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Benchmarks that isolate API tool use from document retrieval or evaluate only final answers without replaying executable tool trajectories.

analysis.tldr: VAKRA is an executable benchmark for agents that must combine structured API calls with document retrieval and obey natural-language tool-use policies, using a fixed ReAct harness and tool-call re-execution to expose cross-source reasoning failures.
analysis.problem: Most agent benchmarks separate API interaction, document retrieval, and policy compliance, making it hard to see whether a model can compose them into one reliable information-acquisition trajectory.
analysis.core_idea: Provide thousands of executable APIs across many domains plus document collections, construct increasingly compositional tasks, re-execute predicted tool calls for correctness, and use a fixed ReAct harness so differences primarily reflect model capability rather than changing agent architecture.
analysis.agent_loop: Interpret task/policy → choose API or document retrieval action → observe structured/unstructured evidence → resolve entities and compose sources → continue or abstain → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The benchmark includes multi-source tasks where the agent must decide which source to use and integrate document retrieval with API observations under natural-language constraints; retrieval is therefore part of the evaluated policy rather than a fixed preprocessing step.
analysis.evidence: The paper reports more than 8,000 executable APIs across 62 domains and evaluates frontier/open-weight models with a fixed ReAct harness. The best model reaches 70.4% on single-hop endpoint-style tasks but about 50–51% on compositional APIs; performance falls sharply with reasoning depth, and some policy-constrained unanswerable cases fall to 2.4%. Trace analysis attributes many failures to entity disambiguation and cross-source grounding rather than tool invocation mechanics.
analysis.why_it_matters: VAKRA shifts evaluation closer to the setting Agentic RAG systems claim to solve: information has to be acquired across heterogeneous sources under execution and policy constraints. It also warns that improving tool-call syntax alone may miss the dominant failure surface.
limitations: A fixed ReAct harness deliberately isolates model capability, so VAKRA does not establish which alternative planning, memory, or retrieval controller would repair the failures.
The benchmark's enterprise-like APIs and document collections are more controlled than noisy open-web environments.
Aggregate trajectory failures bundle entity resolution, source selection, policy interpretation, retrieval, and synthesis; further interventions are needed to causally isolate each control failure.
